statement_scope: Whole original21.12: for fixed nonprincipal U on omega, assume each element of B belongs to a subgroup of B that is a homomorphic image of Z^omega/U. Must B be a homomorphic image of a group ultraproduct modulo the same U? Corson Question3 explicitly identifies Bergman Question19 and supplies a negative example that is not an image of any nonprincipal countable group ultraproduct, covering the original fixed-U conclusion without changing its assumptions.
